q: A woman says, 'Give one hundred dinars to so-and-so and I will be betrothed to you.' What does Rava rule?
options: Betrothed, like a guarantor who binds himself without benefit
why: A guarantor obligates himself though the loan goes to another; so she transfers herself though the money goes to someone else.

q: A man gives a woman money and says, 'Be betrothed with this to so-and-so.' Is she betrothed to so-and-so?
options: Yes, like a Canaanite slave freed by someone else's money
Only if so-and-so later agrees to pay
why: A slave acquires himself when another pays his master; so so-and-so acquires her though he lost nothing.

q: A woman gives a man money and says, 'I will be betrothed to you.' When is she betrothed, according to Mar Zutra?
options: When he is an *adam chashuv*: his accepting her gift is itself a benefit to her
Only if he returns the money
why: An important man doesn't normally accept gifts; her pleasure at his accepting is worth at least a *perutah*.

q: 'Be betrothed to half of me' works, but 'half of you is betrothed to me' does not. Why (Rava)?
options: A man may have two wives, but a woman may not have two husbands
The verse requires a whole woman
why: Betrothing half of her would leave the other half for another man.

q: Why doesn't 'half of you' spread through the whole woman, as consecrating an animal's leg makes the whole animal an *olah*?
options: She has a mind of her own, and consented only to what was offered
A woman can live without half her body
why: An animal has no *da'at*; the woman's consent must reach the betrothal, and it covered only 'half'.

q: How are most of the questions on 7b, such as 'half of you today and half tomorrow', resolved?
options: She is betrothed only if both halves are given the same day
why: Rava's ladder of halves, the two daughters with one *perutah*, and the daughter with a cow or land all end in *teiku*.

q: A man betroths with silk and says, 'It is worth fifty,' but it is not. What is the law?
options: All agree she is not betrothed
Betrothed if it is worth a *perutah*
why: He misstated its value, so she didn't agree to what she got.

options: An appraisal of an item's value
why: Rabba and Rav Yosef dispute when silk of uncertain value must be appraised before it betroths.

q: In the other version, why does Rav Yosef require appraisal even for 'whatever it is worth'?
options: *Shaveh kesef* must have a set value, like money
why: Learned from redeeming a Hebrew slave: grain and vessels worth a *perutah* don't redeem, because they lack a defined value.
